15 EXEMPTIONS

Section 2.0, "Exemptions," of Part V, "Non-Applicabilities and Exemptions," (ML26261A427) of
the Long Mott Generating Station (LMGS) construction permit (CP) application requested the
NRC to grant exemptions from the following regulations upon the initiative of the Commission:

   •   10 CFR 50.34(a)(4)
   •   Regulatory definitions for safety-related (SR) structures, systems, and components
       (SSCs), reactor coolant pressure boundary, safe shutdown, and important to safety (ITS)
       SSCs

Section 2.0 of Part V of the application also includes LME requests for exemptions from the
following regulations:

   •   10 CFR 50.33(f)(1) and 10 CFR 50, Append ix C - financial qualifications
   •   10 CFR 50.34(a)(1)(ii)(D) - analyses of postulated fission product releases
   •   10 CFR 50.68 - criticality safety
   •   10 CFR 26.4(f) - construction fitness for duty

15.1   Analysis and Evaluation of Emergency Core Cooling System (ECCS) Performance
15.1.1 Summary of Exemption
Section 2.1.1 , "10 CFR 50 .34(a)(4) - Analysis of Emergency Core Cooling System (ECCS)
Performance," of Part V, "Non-Applicabilities and Exemptions," (ML26261A427) of the LMGS
CP application identifies portions of 10 CFR 50.34(a)(4) as required for the preliminary safety
analysis report (PSAR). The LMGS CP application requests that the Commission grant an
exemption upon its initiative and states that, "The portions of 10 CFR 50.34(a)(4) requiring
analysis and evaluation of [ECCS] performance in accordance with 10 CFR 50.46 is applicable
to [light water reactors (LWRs)] and is not technically relevant to the LMGS non-LWR design."

15.1.2 Evaluation of Exemption
Authorized by Law

The NRC staff finds that granting of an exemption from the ECCS performance requirements in
10 CFR 50.34(a)(4) will not result in a violation of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended
(hereafter referred to as the AEA), or the Energy Reorganization Act of 1979, as amended
(hereafter referred to as the ERA). In addition , granting of an exemption from the ECCS
performance requirements in 10 CFR 50.34(a)(4) will not result in a violation of the
Commission's regulations because pursuant to 10 CFR 50.12, the Commission may, upon
application by any interested person or upon its own initiative, grant exemptions from the
requirements of 10 CFR Part 50.

Will not Present an Undue Risk to Public Health and Safety

The guidance in DANU-ISG-2022-01 , "Review of Risk-Informed, Technology-Inclusive
Advanced Reactor Applications-Roadmap," (ML23277 A 139), Appendix B, "Analysis of
Applicability of NRC Regulations to Non-Light-Water Power Reactors," Table 6, "Regulations
Referencing Part 50 Regulations Limited to LWRs," states that, 'The second sentence of [1 0
CFR 50.34(a)(4) and 10 CFR 50.34(b)(4)] requires a description of the analysis and evaluation
of the ECCS cooling performance in accordance with 10 CFR 50.46, which is only applicable to
LWRs." Accordingly, the NRC staff finds that granting the exemption from the ECCS
performance requirements in 10 CFR 50.34(a)(4) will not present an undue risk to public health
and safety because the requirement is not applicable to the LMGS design.

Consistent with Common Defense and Security

The ECCS performance requirements in 10 CFR 50.34(a)(4) involve a design feature that is not
applicable to the LMGS design and, therefore, does not affect design, function, or operation of
any structures or plant equipment that is necessary to maintain a secure plant status. In
addition, the requirements are not related to plant security or safeguards procedures or
features. Therefore, as required by 10 CFR 50.12(a)(1), the staff finds that the exemption is
consistent with the common defense and security.

Special Circumstances are Present

Special circumstances, in accordance with 10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(ii), are present whenever
application of the regulation in the particular circumstances would not serve the underlying
purpose of the rule or is not necessary to achieve the underlying purpose of the rule. The
underlying purpose of 10 CFR 50 .34(a)(4) is to provide assurance of adequate core cooling
under accident conditions. The LMGS design, as described in the PSAR, performs the required
safety function of controlling heat removal without the use of an ECCS, which is only required
for LWRs. Accordingly, the NRC staff finds that special circumstances are present under 10
CFR 50.12(a)(2)(ii) because the requirement is not necessary to achieve the underlying purpose
of the rule.

15.1.3 Conclusion
Based upon the discussion above, the NRC staff determined that an exemption to the second
sentence of 10 CFR 50.34(a)(4), requiring a description of the analysis and evaluation of the
ECCS cooling performance in accordance with 10 CFR 50.46, is acceptable because it is
authorized by law, will not present undue risk to public health and safety, is consistent with
common defense and security, and special circumstances are present.

15.2   Definitions
Section 2.1.2, "Regulatory Defin itions," of Part V, "Non-Applicabilities and Exemptions," of the
LMGS CP application requests that the Commission grant, on its own initiative, exemptions to
the regulations that use 10 CFR 50.2 definitions for safety-related (SR) structures systems and
components (SSCs), safety-related electrical equipment, reactor coolant pressure boundary
(RCPB), safe shutdow n, and important to safety (ITS). LME states that these are LWR-centric
definitions and proposes to use alternative definitions that are aligned with the LMGS design
and Nuclear Energy Institute (NEI) 18-04 framework. Because this exemption is being granted
under the Commission's initiative, the information provided in Section 2.1 .2 of Part V of the

application was used to inform the NRC staff's decisions but unless otherwise stated does not
form the basis for the NRC staff's decisions.
The NRC staff identified instances where the definitions of SR SSCs, SR electrical equipment,
RCPB, safe shutdown, and ITS appear in the regulations. The NRC staff evaluated the
applicability of those regulations to the LMGS CP application and identified the exemptions
warranted at the CP stage.

Safety-Related Structures, Systems, and Components

SR SSCs are defined for 10 CFR Part 26 in 10 CFR 26.5, and the term SR appears in §§ 26.3,
26.4, 26.403, 26.405, 26.406, 26.407, 26.409, and 26.419. These regulations are all applicable
to LMGS' application.

In 10 CFR Part 50, the term is defined in 10 CFR 50 .2 and appears without further definition in
§§ 50 .10, 50.55a, 50.69, Appendix B, Appendix R, and Appendix S. The same language used in
the 10 CFR 50 .2 definition of SR SSCs is also used in the 10 CFR 50.49(b )(1) definition of SR
electrical equ ipment, the 10 CFR 50.65(b)(1) definition of SR SSCs within the scope of
maintenance monitoring programs required by 10 CFR 50.65(a)(1), and in the 10 CFR Part 50
Appendix S definition of SSCs requ ired to withstand the effects of the safe shutdown
earthquake (SSE). Of these, 10 CFR 50.2, 50.10, 50.69, Appendix B, and Appendix Sare
applicable to LMGS' application; the reference to SR SSCs in 10 CFR 50.55a is not applicable
to non-LWRs and 10 CFR 50.49 and 50.65 are not applicable to CPs.

The definition of SR SSCs for 10 CFR Part 73 is the same as the 10 CFR Part 50 definition, as
stated in 10 CFR 73.2. In 10 CFR Part 73, the term SR appears in§§ 73.22, 73.54, and 73.77.
Of these, only 10 CFR 73.22 is applicable to CPs.

Because the NRC staff identified several applicable regulations that use the term safety-related
SSCs, the NRC staff initiated an exemption as detailed below.

Safety-Related Electrical Equipment

SR electrical equipment is defined in 10 CFR 50.49(b)(1)(i) with a definition that is identical to
the definition of SR SSCs in 10 CFR 50 .2. However, 10 CFR 50.49 is not applicable to CP
applications. As such, the staff did not consider exemptions to 10 CFR 50.49 in the scope of the
NRC-initiated exemption discussed here.

Reactor Coolant Pressure Boundary

RCPB is defined in 10 CFR 50.2 in relation to "pressure-retaining components of boiling and
pressurized water-cooled nuclear power reactors." RCPB appears in regulations that are
applicable to the LMGS application (a non-LWR applying for a CP) in the definition of SR SSCs
and basic component in 10 CFR 50 .2 and the definition of SSCs required to withstand the
effects of the SSE in 10 CFR 50 Appendix S. Because the only applicable regulations that use
RCPB use the term in a manner that is the same way it is used in the definition of SR SSCs in
10 CFR 50.2, the NRC staff is considering these regulations under the safety-related exemption
and is not considering a separate exemption from the definition of RCPB.

Safe Shutdown



                                              15-3

                       OliiliilCIAb U&I! ONbX   PROPRll!+ARV INliiORMi".+ION


A general definition of the term safe shutdown is not provided in 10 CFR Part 50. 10 CFR 50.2
provides a definition for "safe shutdown (non-design basis accident (OBA))" specifically as it
relates to station blackout conditions, but the requirement under 10 CFR 50 .63 to consider
station blackout is itself only applicable to LWRs. It is therefore acceptable for the applicant to
identify an appropriate definition of safe shutdown consistent with applicable NRC policy and
guidance to use where necessary in demonstrating compliance with the regulations. However,
the NRC staff notes that the only instances of the term "safe shutdown" in the 10 CFR Part 50
regulations that are applicable to the LMGS CP application are in the context of the definition of
safety-related equipment (or other terms that use the same definition, as discussed above) that
are covered by the NRC-initiated exemption. Other instances are not applicable to new reactors,
non-LWRs, or CP applicants. As such the NRC staff did not consider a separate exemption
related to the definition of safe shutdown.

Important to Safety

The introduction to 10 CFR 50 Append ix A provides a definition of "important to safety" as
"structures, systems, and components that provide reasonable assurance that the facility can be
operated without undue risk to the health and safety of the public." The NRC staff notes that 10
CFR 50.49(b) provides a more specific definition of "electrical equipment important to safety" as
SR electrical equipment (following the same definition as in 10 CFR 50.2 for SR SSCs) plus
certain non-SR electrical equipment. However, 10 CFR 50.49 is not applicable to CP applicants.
As noted in DANU-ISG-2022-01 and Regulatory Guide (RG ) 1.253, SSCs classified as SR and
NSRST under the NEI 18-04 process are considered important to safety. In section 2.1.2.4 of
Part V of the application, LME described that "important to safety" SSCs for LMGS includes all
SR and NSRST SSCs, consistent with the discussion in DANU-ISG-2022-01 and RG 1.253. As
such , the NRC staff did not consider an exemption to apply an alternate definition of the term
"important to safety" to be necessary for LMGS.

15.2.1 Summary of Exemption
LME uses the guidance in NEI 18-04, Rev. 1, as endorsed by RG 1.233, Rev. 0
(ML20091 L620), to perform the safety classification of SSCs. Following this process, SSCs and
associated functions may have different safety classifications than those based on the 10 CFR
26.5 and 10 CFR 50.2 definitions of safety-related SSCs. The NEI 18-04 approach to SSC
classification is a risk-informed, performance-based , and technology-inclusive means of
identifying safety-sign ificant SSCs at the facility. Regulatory position C.2 of RG 1.233 states, in
part, that use of the term "safety-related" in NEI 18-04 is not the same as the 10 CFR 50.2
definition, that SSCs included in the "safety-related" classification for non-LWRs may not be the
same as those considered safety-related for LWRs, and that applicants are expected to identify
exceptions to and exemptions needed from NRC regulations. The NRC staff considers it
appropriate for a non-LWR applicant to use the NEI 18-04 process to address whether an SSC
should be considered safety-significant, based on the acceptability of the NEI 18-04 process as
discussed in RG 1.233. Therefore, the NRC staff identified and concluded that granting an
exemption from certain requirements related to the 10 CFR 26.5 and 10 CFR 50 .2 definition of
safety-related SSCs was warranted.

Though definitions themselves do not create requirements, the use of an alternate definition
necessitates an exemption from the regulations where that definition is used.

applicant:

The alternate definition of safety-related SSCs for that in 10 CFR 50.2 will be as follows for the

       systems and components classified as safety-related in accordance with NEI 18-

       Regulatory Gu ide 1.233, "Guidance for a Technology-Inclusive, Risk-Informed,

       of Applications for Licenses, Certifications, and Approvals for Non-Light-Water
       Reactors," Revision 0.

The alternate definition of "structures, systems, and components required to withstand the
effects of the safe-shutdown earthquake ground motion or surface deformation" for that in 10
CFR 50 Append ix S will be as follows for the applicant:

       Structures, systems, and components required to withstand the effects of the

The NRC staff identified where the definition for "safety-related SSCs," is used in the regulations
that apply the same language as those definitions, and regulations that refer to safety-related
SSCs in 10 CFR parts 26, 50, and 73 that are relevant to a CP application. The following
sections describe the regulations affected by the exemption :

1O CFR Part 26, "Fitness for Duty Programs"
10 CFR 26.3, "Scope," defines the scope of fitness for duty program requirements.

10 CFR 26.3(c)(4) specifies that the scope includes construction permit holder (under 10 CFR
Part 50) and makes several references to SR SSCs.

10 CFR 26.405, "Drug and alcohol testing," provides requirements related to drug and alcohol

10 CFR 26.407, "Behavioral observations," provides a requirement for individuals involved in

1O CFR 26.409, "Sanctions," requires licensees and other entities implementing an FFD

10 CFR 26.419, "Suitability and fitness evaluations," provides a requirement for licensees and

1O CFR Part 50, "Domestic Licensing of Production and Utilization Facilities"

to assure:

    (1) The integrity of the reactor coolant pressure boundary;

   (2) The capability to shut down the reactor and maintain it in a safe shutdown condition;

10 CFR 50, Appendix S, "Earthquake Engineering Criteria for Nuclear Power Plants," Il l,

Appendix S, Section IV , "Application to Engineering Design," also states the following relative to

    (a)(1) Safe Shutdown Earthquake Ground Motion .



       (ii) The nuclear power plant must be designed so that, if the Safe Shutdown Earthquake

1O CFR Part 73, "Physical protection of plants and materials"

10 CFR 73.22, "Protection of Safeguards Information: Specific requirements," provides

15.2.2 Evaluation of Exemption
Exemption from 10 CFR Part 26
Pursuant to 10 CFR 26.9, "Specific exemptions," the Commission may, on its own initiative,
grant exemptions from the requ irements of 10 CFR Part 26 as it determines are authorized by
law, will not endanger life or property or the common defense and security, and are otherwise in
the public interest.
Authorized by Law
The scope of SSCs considered to be SR is not defined in the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as
amended, or the Energy Reorganization Act of 1974, as amended. The identified exemption in
this instance is authorized by law, because no other prohibition of law exists to preclude the
activities which would be authorized by the exemption . Additionally, 10 CFR 26.9 allows the
Commission to, on its own initiative, grant exemptions from the requirements of 10 CFR Part 26
if the Commission makes certain findings.
As such , the NRC staff has determined that granting an exemption from the requirement to
apply the substantive regulations to safety-related SSCs meeting the definition in 10 CFR Part
26 for the purpose of complying with the above stated regulations in 10 CFR Part 26 and
instead, use the alternate definition provided above, when identifying safety-related SSCs in the
sections of 10 CFR Part 26 identified above will not result in a violation of any Act or the
Commission's regulations. Therefore, the exemption is authorized by law.
Will not Endanger Life or Property
As stated in RG 1.233, the NEI 18-04 definition of safety-related SSCs differs from that provided
in the regulations, but "the methods described in NEI 18-04 constitute one acceptable means
to .. . classify SSCs." RG 1.233 further states that the purpose of the safety classification aspect
of NEI 18-04 is to ensure "applicants provide the necessary capabilities to perform mitigation
functions and ensure the reliability of SSCs to prevent LBEs with more severe consequences"
and "determine if special treatments beyond normal industrial practices are needed to ensure
SSC performance of safety functions in the prevention and mitigation of LBEs." As discussed in
NEI 18-04, these special treatments include provisions for the design, construction, installation,
operation, and maintenance of SSCs that provide increased assurance beyond normal industrial
practices that SSCs perform their design-basis functions.
Though the NEI 18-04 definition differs from the 10 CFR 26.5 definition of safety-related SSCs,
it is consistent with the underlying purpose of identifying those SSCs that are most safety-
significant to ensure they have adequate assurance that they can perform their design-basis

functions. A more comprehensive evaluation of the NEI 18-04 definition of safety-related and its
consistency with public health and safety is provided below with respect to the definition
provided in 10 CFR 50 .2 (which is identical to that provided in 10 CFR 26.5). The above 10 CFR
Part 26 regulations to which this exemption would apply are related to the FFD program . This
exemption would ensure that the FFD program applies to the most safety-significant SSCs,
which is consistent with the underlying intent of the definition of safety-related SSCs in 10 CFR
Part 26.
As discussed in PSAR section 5.1.1 and evaluated in section 5.1.1 of this SE, LME deviates
from staff position C.2 in RG 1.233 for the safety classification of SSCs providing a load path for
SR SSCs, which should be classified in a manner consistent with the higher-level function they
are supporting (i. e., SR) but are classified as risk-significant NSRST by LME with add itional
treatments applied to ensure they can perform their safety-significant function . As discussed in
section 5. 1.1 of this SE, the foundations of these structures are still within the scope of the FFD
program because the definition of constructing or construction activities in 10 CFR Part 26
explicitly includes installation of the foundations, including concrete, for safety-related SSCs. As
such , the proposed exemption will not endanger life or property because safety-related SSCs
will continue to be defined using a process the NRC staff has determined to be acceptable and
will remain subject to appropriate fitness-for-duty programs to ensure they are constructed
appropriately.
Will not Endanger the Common Defense and Security
The exemption does not affect requirements in 10 CFR Part 26 related to nuclear power reactor
security; therefore, this exemption will not endanger the common defense and security.
Requirements in 10 CFR Part 73 that are affected by the exemption and which could relate to
the common defense and security are evaluated below.
In the public interest
The FFD program ensures that personnel are fit to safely and competently perform their duties.
This exemption is in the public interest because it would ensure that the FFD program applies to
the most safety-significant SSCs.
Exemption from 10 CFR Part 50

Pursuant to 10 CFR 50. 12, the NRC may, upon application by any interested person or upon its
own initiative, grant exemptions from the requirements of 10 CFR Part 50 when: (1) the
exemptions are authorized by law, will not present an undue risk to the public health or safety,
and are consistent with the common defense and security; and (2) when special circumstances
are present. Under 10 CFR 50.12(a)(2), special circumstances include, among other things,
when application of the specific regulation in the particular circumstances would not serve, or is
not necessary to achieve, the underlying purpose of the rule.

Authorized by Law

The scope of SSCs considered to be SR is not defined in the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as
amended, or the Energy Reorganization Act of 1974, as amended. The identified exemption in
this instance is authorized by law, because no other prohibition of law exists to preclude the
activities which would be authorized by the exemption . Additionally, 10 CFR 50.12 allows the
Commission to, on its own initiative, grant exemptions from the requirements of 10 CFR Part 50
if the Commission makes certain findings.


                                               15-9

As such, the NRC staff has determined that granting an exemption from the requirement to
apply the substantive regulations to safety-related SSCs meeting the definition in 10 CFR Part
50 for the purpose of complying with the above stated regulations in 10 CFR Part 50 and
instead, use the alternate definition provided above, when identifying safety-related SSCs in the
sections of 10 CFR Part 50 identified above will not result in a violation of any Act or the
Commission's regulations. Therefore, the exemption is authorized by law.

Will not Present an Undue Risk to Public Health and Safety

Though the NEI 18-04 definition differs from the 10 CFR 50.2 definition of SR SSCs, it is
consistent with the underlying purpose of identifying SSCs that are the most safety-significant to
ensure they have adequate assurance that they can perform their design-basis functions. The
10 CFR 50.2 definition of "safety-related" contains three elements which , as noted above, relate
to the maintaining the integrity of the RCPB, achieving and maintaining safe shutdown, and
preventing and mitigating radiological consequences of accidents. With respect to the first and
second elements, the NEI 18-04 process includes the evaluation and classification of those
SSCs necessary to support three fundamental safety functions (FSFs). including control of heat
generation, control of heat removal, and radionuclide retention. The NEI 18-04 process
evaluates the SSCs necessary to achieve these FSFs and classifies them as SR if they are

criterion are classified as SR. Based on this, the staff determined that the NEI 18-04 process
includes appropriate consideration of the key elements of the 10 CFR 50.2 definition of safety-
related, particularly including the consequences of accidents. As such the staff concluded that
replacing this portion of the 10 CFR 50.2 definition with the NEI 18-04 definition of safety-
related, as delineated above for the applicant, would not present an undue risk to public health
and safety.

The purpose of 10 CFR 50 .10 is to define construction (10 CFR 50.1 0(a)); to provide a
requirement for a license for production and utilization facilities (10 CFR 50.10(b)); to specify
that construction cannot begin until a construction permit, combined license, early site permit, or
limited work authorization (LWA) is issued (10 CFR 50.1 0(c)); to provide requirements
concerning the request for, issuance of, and effect of LWAs (10 CFR 50 .10(d) through (f)); and
to provide requirements for implementation of a redress plan (10 CFR 50 .10(g)). The current
action would provide LME with a CP for LMGS, with the find ing that construction would not
present an undue risk to public health and safety pursuant to 10 CFR 50 .35(a)(4)(ii) and
enabling construction activities to commence. As such, this exemption does not present an
undue risk to public health and safety as it relates to 10 CFR 50.10.

10 CFR 50.69 is a voluntary alternative to compliance with several regulations and is not
identified in the LMGS application. Because of this, the NRC staff did not consider it in the
present evaluation.

Regarding Appendix B to 10 CFR Part 50, using an alternate definition of SR SSCs does not
affect the need for quality assurance (QA) for SSCs that "prevent or mitigate the consequences
of postulated accidents that could cause undue risk to the health and safety of the public."

15.4 Analysis of Postulated Fission Product Release
15.4.1 Summary of Exemption
In Section 2.2.2, "1O CFR 50.34(1)(ii ) (0) -Analysis of Postulated Fission Product Release," of

result of a "major accident," which per Footnote 6 of Paragraph (a)(1)(ii)(O) is assumed to be an

means for a non-LWR applicant using the LMP-based methodology to address the requirements
of 10 CFR 50 .34(a)(1)(ii)(O).

15.6.2 Evaluation of Exemption
Authorized by Law

The NRC staff has determined that granting of the applicant's proposed exemption will not result
in a violation of the AEA, as amended, or the ERA, as amended. In addition , granting of the
applicant's proposed exemptions will not result in a violation of the Commission's regulations
because pursuant to 10 CFR 26.9, the Commission may, upon application by any interested
person or upon its own initiative, grant exemptions from the requirements of 10 CFR Part 26.

Will not Endanger Life or Property or the Common Defense and Security

The exemption enables the escorting of temporary construction workers performing duties
under 1O CFR 26.4(f). The exemption does not change any SSC, any existing natural or man-
made geological/biological feature, or other material property on the construction site, nor does
the exemption introduce any new industrial, chemical, or radiological hazard that would present
itself as a latent or apparent adverse effect on life or property. The exemption also does not
request any relaxation in work controls, processes, quality assurance, quality verification, or the
training, qualification , and personal injury protections afforded to individuals constructing or
directing the construction of safety- or security-related SSCs.

Otherwise in the Public Interest

The NRC staff finds that it is in the public's interest that LME be allowed to escort certain
individuals who direct or perform 10 CFR 26.4(f) duties and responsibilities because the
proposed exemption has a direct nexus to improve flexibility in construction scheduling, work
planning, and conduct of construction activities. These improvements occurs because the
exemption would enable LME to implement process and procedural changes in a manner that
leverages immediately available construction workers for short duration construction activities
without a reduction in the assurance of public health and safety or the common defense and
security because of the LME-proposed administrative controls for its escort program.

15.6.3 Conclusion
The NRC staff finds that the partial exemption to 1O CFR 26.4(f), as described in Section 2.2.4
of Part V of the LMGS CP application (ML26261A427) is acceptable because it is authorized by
